key_insight: SpecGP is a transformer-based model that predicts energy-adaptable N‑glycopeptide structural spectra with enhanced fragment‑ion coverage, enabling improved isomer discrimination and higher identification confidence via rescoring.
problem_solved: Mass‑spectrometry identification of N‑glycopeptides suffers from variable collision energies and sparse/uncertain fragment ion coverage, which limits the ability to distinguish isomeric glycoforms and reduces confidence in identifications.
method: Transformer architecture that conditions spectral predictions on collision/activation energy to produce energy‑adaptable spectra.
Structural‑aware representation of glycopeptides (peptide + glycan) to boost predicted fragment‑ion coverage across both peptide- and glycan-derived ions.
Integration of predicted spectra into rescoring workflows to improve isomer discrimination and overall identification confidence.
impact: Provides a practical AI tool for glycoproteomics pipelines: ML practitioners can adopt energy‑conditioned spectral predictors to increase identification accuracy, guide targeted experiments, and improve downstream rescoring and analysis.
visual_elements: Model architecture diagram: transformer encoder/decoder with an energy conditioning input and peptide+glycan embedding streams.
Heatmap or line plots: predicted vs observed spectral intensity across a range of collision energies to show energy adaptability.
Before/after bar chart: identification accuracy and isomer discrimination rates with and without SpecGP rescoring.
Fragment coverage schematic: cartoons showing increased peptide and glycan fragment ions predicted by SpecGP vs baseline.
paper_title: SpecGP as a transformer-based model for predicting energy-adaptable structural spectra of glycopeptides
paper_authors: Xianyong Wang, Rui Song, Zhuangzhuang Feng, Shisheng Sun
